title: NSFlow: An End-to-End FPGA Framework with Scalable Dataflow Architecture for Neuro-Symbolic AI
problem: Neuro-Symbolic AI workloads exhibit heterogeneous kernels and unique memory access patterns unsuitable for general-purpose ML accelerators (CPU/GPU/TPU).
motivation: NSAI systems integrate neural networks and symbolic reasoning; their distinctive computation and memory patterns require specialized acceleration.
method: NSFlow features a design architecture generator identifying data dependencies and creating optimized dataflows, plus a reconfigurable FPGA array with flexible compute units, reorganizable memory, and mixed-precision capabilities.
key_novelty: Architecture generator synthesizing optimized FPGA dataflows from NSAI workload data dependencies, enabling end-to-end acceleration.
contributions: Design architecture generator identifying workload dependencies and creating optimized dataflow architectures
Reconfigurable FPGA array with flexible compute units, memory reorganization, and mixed-precision
31x speedup over Jetson TX2, >2x over GPU, 8x over TPU-like systolic array, >3x over Xilinx DPU
Enhanced scalability: only 4x runtime increase when symbolic workloads scale by 150x

metrics.speedup: 31x vs Jetson TX2, >2x vs GPU, 8x vs TPU, >3x vs Xilinx DPU

limitations: FPGA resource utilization and scalability to very large NSAI models not thoroughly analyzed.
primary_theme: FPGA dataflow framework for neuro-symbolic AI acceleration
